mechanism_reasoning: mimic-driven miR-181b overexpression: STAT3 transactivates the regulatory RNA miR-181b, which pairs with the CYLD 3'UTR and loads RISC/AGO2 to degrade CYLD mRNA, so extra miR-181b indirectly lowers CYLD; STAT3's repression of CYLD is relayed through this intermediate microRNA (regulatory RNA-mediated indirect regulation).

BHLHE40 overexpression: the bHLH corepressor BHLHE40 is recruited to PPARα-bound regulatory regions of Pdk4 and delivers HDAC corepressor activity that deacetylates local histones and closes the chromatin template, so PPARα-driven Pdk4 transcription falls; the TF-target effect requires this chromatin regulator acting downstream of PPARA binding (chromatin-mediated regulation).

miR-10b inhibition by antagomir/inhibitor: TWIST1-induced miR-10b is the repressive intermediate that binds the HOXD10 3'UTR and silences it, so sequestering miR-10b releases HOXD10 from RISC repression and HOXD10 rises; TWIST1's control of HOXD10 is relayed through this microRNA (regulatory RNA-mediated indirect regulation).

PPARA overexpression: excess PPARα binds the PPRE cis-element in the Angptl4 enhancer/promoter and directly activates transcription, so Angptl4 rises; the effect runs through a target-linked cis-regulatory DNA element with no intermediate required (direct cis-regulatory DNA regulation).

PPARA overexpression: excess PPARα occupies the PPRE cis-element in the Hmgcs2 promoter/enhancer and directly drives transcription, so Hmgcs2 rises; the effect acts through a target-linked cis-regulatory DNA element with no intermediate factor (direct cis-regulatory DNA regulation).

NOTCH1 knockdown: SMAD3-driven activation of PTPRK requires NOTCH1 as a cooperating partner at the locus, so losing NOTCH1 (NICD-CSL) disables the combinatorial complex and PTPRK falls even though SMAD3 itself is intact; the SMAD3-to-PTPRK effect depends on this partner transcription factor (combinatorial TF regulation).

SMAD3 knockdown: depleting the TF itself removes SMAD3 occupancy of SBE cis-elements in the PTPRK regulatory region, so direct promoter/enhancer activation is lost and PTPRK transcription drops; the effect is mediated by a target-linked cis-regulatory DNA element (direct cis-regulatory DNA regulation).

SMAD4 knockdown: SMAD3 must heterodimerize with the co-SMAD partner SMAD4 to form a productive DNA-binding complex, so removing SMAD4 leaves SMAD3 unable to activate PTPRK and the target falls; PTPRK expression requires this partner transcription factor (combinatorial TF regulation).

Combined overexpression of NOTCH1 and TGF-beta/SMAD3: NICD-CSL and SMAD3 co-occupy the PTPRK locus and co-activate it, so raising both partners together drives PTPRK up; the target requires the cooperating factor pair rather than either partner alone (combinatorial TF regulation).
